item.title: Yaprr 0.5.0
item.description:
• The mic starts in about 80 ms: Yaprr gets the mic ready while idle, so pressing the key only has to start it (it used to take half a second to a second). It shows "listening" straight away, and "waking up" only for a mic that's slow to send sound. Letting go closes the mic at once unless you're mid-word.
  • Pick any key for talking and hands-free: Settings records the hold-to-talk and double-tap keys: either side of any modifier, fn, or a combo like ⌃⌥Space. Hands-free switches off if it clashes with the talk key, and every label in the app shows the keys you picked.
  • "Are your headphones on?" Bluetooth headphones that send sound but no words (many mute their mic when not worn) now get that question, with Try again and Switch mic, instead of a quick "Didn't catch that".
  • The indicator's hover menu has Quit.
  • A proper install window: Yaprr.dmg opens on a Yaprr background with one arrow from the app to Applications, the steps to open it, and how to get past the first-launch block.
  • Getting started checklist: after the tour, a "Getting started" pill sits in the window's corner with seven things worth doing first: set up, say your first yap, tell Yaprr what you do, go hands-free, fix a word where it landed, teach a style, and log in. Each ticks itself off when you do it. Hide it for now, or bring it back (and replay the tour) from Help → Getting started, which also has the "Good to know before you yap" list.
  • If a setup step stops working (say Accessibility gets turned off), a red bar across the window says what broke, with a Fix it button.
  • New-feature dots: after an update, a pulsing dot in your vibe's color marks pages with something new, until you open them.
  • Notices got a makeover: each one has an icon in a color that says what it's about (mint for done, lavender for info, yellow for a heads-up, coral for a problem), a bold title and a line of detail. "Picked up words from your apps" links to Dictionary, and notices stay up long enough to read (2.5 to 5 seconds).
  • "You're on <version>" after an update, with a link to what's new in it.
  • Turning on "Send text before my cursor" first shows exactly what's sent to Alpie Seed (up to 300 characters before the cursor, the app name and window title) and what never is (anything after the cursor, your audio).
  • Fixed: Help's GitHub and Report a bug buttons opened a page you couldn't see. They're gone; Send a report, right below, reaches the person who builds Yaprr.
  • Fixed: the command-line test tools in the README (`--format`, `--learn`, `--transcribe`) couldn't start since 0.4.0, because they couldn't find the update framework.
